summary: Nirmal Chandra Sinha was a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology who studied at the University of Calcutta and Presidency University. He worked at the National Archives of India, Krishnath College, University of Calcutta, and served as founder director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology.
Nirupam Chakma specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts degree at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Tilak Kariyawasam and Fa Qing (attested 2015).
Nitin Kumar Jain is an Indologist who earned his PhD at Central Sanskrit University, where he also served as an assistant professor in 2019.
Nivitigala Sumitta Thero is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned a PhD at the University of the West (2014–2023). He founded and served as CEO of Dhamma USA in 2022.
Noa Gal specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. Gal studied at the University of Oxford under doctoral supervisor Richard Gombrich, receiving a Doctor of Philosophy degree (attested 2003).

Noa Ronkin is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. She studied under Shlomo Biderman and completed a D.Phil. at Wolfson College, Oxford, under Richard Gombrich in 2003, later serving as lecturer and research fellow at Stanford University.
Noah Avigan works in the fields of Indology and religious studies. He is a graduate student and affiliated with the Department of Religious Studies at Yale University (attested 2026).

Noboru Karashima was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who completed his degrees at the University of Tokyo. He held faculty posts at the University of Tokyo (emeritus 1981–1994) and Taisho University (~1994–2008), and presided over several international academic associations.

Noboru Miyata was a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and history/archaeology. He studied at Tokyo University of Education and the University of Tsukuba, holding academic posts at Tokyo Gakugei University, the University of Tsukuba, and Kanagawa University.
Noboru Ueda is a scholar in Buddhist studies who held a post at the University of Tokyo (attested 1990) and served as a professor at Mejiro University (attested 2015).

Nobuchiyo Kotani is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Otani University and Kyoto University under Yuichi Kajiyama, Hajime Sakurabe, and Noritoshi Aramaki, later serving as professor at Otani University and president of Otani University Junior College.

Nobuhiko Kobayashi is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied at Kyoto University under Yutaka Ochihara. He held academic posts at the University of Toronto, Kyoto University, and Taisho University.

Nobuhiro Ota is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his undergraduate and doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo and has held academic appointments at the University of Tokyo and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies.
Nobukatsu Komai specializes in Buddhist studies. Komai studied as a research student at Taisho University and served as a full-time researcher at Chisan Denpōin (attested 2014).
Nobumasa Hibi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Rissho University from ~1955 to 1959 and served there as an associate professor from ~1970 to 1978.

Tensho (Nobumasa) Miyazaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned a doctorate at the University of Tokyo, holding appointments at Toyo University, the University of Tokyo, and Tokyo University of Agriculture.

Nobumi Iyanaga is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études. He held academic posts at the University of Tokyo and the École française d'Extrême-Orient, and led the Société Franco-Japonaise des Études Orientales.
Nobuo Otsuka is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral coursework at Taisho University (~1982–1988), where he also held a post as a researcher (attested 1995).

Nobuyoshi Yamabe is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Osaka, Otani, and Yale universities under Noritoshi Aramaki and Stanley Weinstein. He held faculty posts at Kyushu Ryukoku, Tokyo University of Agriculture, and Waseda University.

Nobuyuki Kaji is a scholar of philosophy and Sinology who studied at Kyoto and Tohoku universities. He held academic posts at Koyasan University, Nagoya University, Osaka University, Koshien Junior College, Doshisha University, and Ritsumeikan University.
